description: I'm Amal, a Physics graduate and software developer passionate about space exploration, AI/ML, and planetary science. I bring experience in Python, machine learning, geospatial technologies, and full-stack development. I'm excited to explore Earth analogues for Moon and Mars habitats. I'm looking for teammates with expertise in geology, GIS, remote sensing, astrobiology, aerospace engineering, and robotics who enjoy research, experimentation, and ambitious problem-solving.
summary:
LUXMARTIS helps explorers find Earth places that can stand in for the Moon and Mars. It compares curated terrestrial analog sites with lunar and Martian reference regions using research-backed geological and environmental class codes—not photos, and not AI-generated scores.

Users can search sites, explore separate Lunar and Martian pathways, review feature scores and rankings, and see clear limits on what each comparison can and cannot claim. The platform draws on public archives from NASA, ESA, JAXA, and CSA for discovery and context, while similarity numbers come from a transparent Python comparison engine over a versioned literature registry.

Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, LUXMARTIS treats Earth as a testing ground for planetary exploration—helping scientists, educators, and the public understand where Earth fieldwork can meaningfully inform missions beyond our world
details: LuxMartis is an interactive planetary analog discovery platform that identifies and evaluates locations on Earth with geological and environmental characteristics similar to the Moon and Mars. Using scientific datasets, geospatial analysis, multi-criteria similarity assessment, and immersive 3D visualizations, it helps users discover potential analog environments and understand their relevance to future planetary exploration.
